A fast precursor can mature during ON or within the edge exclusion; a precursor with beta near b0 can be invisible to this comparison. This candidate is not an established novel molecular mechanism.

## Selection, split and frozen rules

Exact manifests: raw/traces_manifest.csv and raw/selected_manifest.csv. There are **44 traces from 43 unique cells**:
- Discovery: 22 traces, 22 cells; 8 assisting, 8 hindering, 6 unforced.
- Validation: 22 traces, 21 cells; 8 assisting, 8 hindering, 6 unforced. One cell appears in both forcing directions.
- No cell identifier crosses the split.

SHA-256 of motor_priming_20261010: plus the source cell ID determines split and ordering. One filename per cell per condition is selected before reading outcomes. Condition-specific rows can therefore share a cell.

PREANALYSIS.md predates raw outcome inspection, although published figures were known. Extraction was developed on discovery and frozen before validation parsing. An initial freeze had a logical error: it could label a brief initial speed excursion an event without the required persistence. Corrected before validation parsing; both sources and hashes are retained. An exploratory plotting sign error is also documented; preliminary plots are not the final analysis.

Frozen observation rule:
- Use the raw long-axis/PCA revolution field at 4 kHz; centroid-angle tracking failed in some discovery traces.
- Normalize sign to each measured 1–9-s baseline, not the forcing label.
- Velocity: degree-1 Savitzky–Golay derivative over 401 samples, then 100-Hz analysis grid.
- Primary activity threshold: 5% baseline; fixed sensitivities 2.5%, 7.5%.
- Persistence: 14 of 15 successive 10-ms samples above threshold.
- Primary edge exclusion 100 ms; sensitivity 200 ms. Both exceed the derivative's ~50-ms lookahead.
- Initial activity or an onset within 50 ms of the guard is immediate/unresolved.
- A resolved later onset additionally requires initial 100-ms mean speed below half threshold and onset at least 100 ms after the guard.
- Stop at the first detected event; later pulses are not independent first arrivals.

Ten synthetic positive/negative-direction cases passed timing/classification checks. This is numerical QA, not biological calibration.

source_excerpts.text:
# Before outcome-trace inspection, 2026-10-10 UTC

Question: Does externally imposed rotor motion instantaneously enable torque-generating stator capture, or first populate a latent mechanically primed state that becomes torque-generating after forcing ends?

Selected evidence: Ito, Nakamura, Toyabe (2021), DOI 10.1038/s41467-021-23516-y. Public figshare 14371232.v2, raw 4000-Hz rotational traces. Article authors already establish rotation-enhanced assembly, suggest gear-driven activation and MotB stretching, and report direction asymmetry. Those facts are prior art, not our invention.

The raw archive directory has been read, but no outcome trace has been inspected as of this document. Published figures and manuscript were examined, so this is an analysis plan, not a preregistration.

Candidate comparison: (i) T-cell optogenetic proofreading has outstanding importance and independently manipulated ligand lifetime, but observed cluster persistence and nucleation-memory mechanisms are already directly anticipated by the papers; reporters are often separate cell populations. (ii) osmotic membrane adaptation has many knockout interventions but many jointly changing hydraulic, ionic and endocytic variables, so mechanism identification is weaker. (iii) motor assembly permits external rotation reversal and pulsed cessation with the same observable on subsecond timescales. Select (iii) on identifiability, not the strongest-sounding anomaly.

Primary candidate, to be falsified: unbound D -> primed P during external motion at rate alpha(direction, speed), then P -> torque-generating A at rate beta, competing P -> D at rate gamma. Motion can prepare a state even while no active stator exists. In an OFF interval with negligible new priming, the extra activation density from P decays with beta+gamma; its lifetime is a physical memory of mechanical exposure. Instantaneous memoryless activation predicts a constant baseline OFF hazard after instrument-edge guard time.

Primary statistic: time of first sustained positive autonomous rotation in OFF intervals, relative to the end of the preceding ON pulse. Compare early versus late OFF hazard using at-risk exposure, censoring, cell-level clustering and guard-time robustness. Distinguish delayed torque onset from delayed attachment, since torque alone cannot observe docking. An early spike confined to the guard zone is an edge
